title: European Version of OpenAI Lands in Singapore: Mistral AI Establishes Asia-Pacific Headquarters to Build Sovereign AI for Asian Governments

content_html:
French AI company Mistral AI has officially anchored its Asian base in Singapore. Last week (November 20), the company announced it would set up its Asia-Pacific headquarters here, with plans to expand its regional workforce to more than 200 people by 2027 and recruit local talent in research, engineering, AI, and robotics. The new office will operate in the form of an “Expanded Science Center,” with a core mission to develop custom AI models for government agencies and industrial clients, focusing on three key areas—the public sector, high-tech manufacturing, and robotics—to build “sovereign AI,” meaning enabling organizations to control critical elements such as process knowledge, intellectual property, data, and product development themselves.

This move was not made hastily. Mistral and Singapore’s Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) already had ties: the two sides signed a memorandum of understanding in November 2025 and signed a master strategic innovation cooperation agreement this April; even earlier, they had jointly advanced the Phoenix project—HTX’s first fully sovereign AI model family, regarded as one of Singapore’s earliest models centered on the nation and the Home Team. This June, the family gained its first multimodal, multilingual member, Phoenix-VL1.5Medium, which can recognize languages commonly used in Singapore and the region and has already been deployed into the Home Team ecosystem. HTX’s frontline departments—the Police Force, the Civil Defence Force, and the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority—are precisely the users this AI is meant to serve.

Robotics is also advancing in parallel. Mistral is developing related intelligent models, among them Robostral Navigate, a fully in-house 8B model that can autonomously navigate complex environments using only a single RGB camera.

Supporting this expansion is Mistral’s steadily rising funding curve. Founded in Paris in April 2023, the company’s three co-founders all come from European AI backgrounds: CEO Arthur Mensch was formerly a senior research scientist at Google DeepMind, while Chief Scientist Guillaume Lample and CTO Timothée Lacroix both worked on LLaMA development at Meta. Just weeks after founding, it secured a €105 million seed round, setting a European record at the time; then a €385 million Series A and a €600 million Series B followed in quick succession; in September 2025, in its €1.7 billion Series C, lithography giant ASML alone invested €1.3 billion and became the largest shareholder with an approximately 11% stake; in September 2026, its €3 billion Series D was co-led by Samsung Electronics, PSG Equity, and Scaleup Europe Fund, lifting its post-money valuation to €21 billion. With its open-weight approach and custom tools such as Forge, the company is now selling “sovereign AI” from Europe to Asia—and Singapore is the first outpost it has extended into the Asia-Pacific.
